en.greeting: Hi, welcome back! Today you build your first real English sentences: who you are, where you're from, and what things are. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: I'm = I am
steps.text: Let's start with you: your name and your city.
steps.body: Indonesian says *Saya Budi*, with nothing in the middle. English needs **am** there (≈ *adalah*): **I am Budi**. When we speak, we usually join them: **I'm** (the **'** replaces the *a*). For your city or country, add **from**: **I'm from Bandung**. Before a job, add **a** (≈ *seorang*): **I'm a student**. Indonesian can drop *seorang*; English can't drop **a**.

steps.title: Introduce yourself
steps.text: Here is how people say their name, job and city.
steps.body: Every sentence starts with **I'm**. Never just *I*.

examples.en: Hi, I'm Sari. I'm a teacher.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Put the words in English order. Who first, then where from.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya dari Makassar.
question.explanation: Start with **I'm** (= I am), then **from** + the city. 'Saya dari Makassar' needs nothing between *Saya* and *dari*, but English needs the **'m** (am).

steps.title: This is … and It's …
steps.text: Now let's talk about things around you.
steps.body: *Ini kunci saya* has nothing between *Ini* and *kunci saya*, but English needs **is**: **This is my key.** Note the order: *kunci saya* → **my key** (*my* first). Use **This is** to show something near you. Then say more about the same thing with **It's** (= it is): **It's small.** Careful: **its** without an apostrophe means '-nya' (belonging to a thing), not 'it is'.

steps.title: Show and tell
steps.text: First show the thing with This is, then describe it with It's.
steps.body: **This is** names the thing. **It's** tells you more about it.

examples.en: This is my phone. It's black.
This is my office. It's small.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Look closely at each sentence. Is the little word **is** there? Is the apostrophe right?

question.prompt: Budi shows his new motorbike. Which is correct?
options: This is my motorbike. It's new.
This is my motorbike. Its new.
question.explanation: Both sentences need **is**: **This is** and **It's** (= it is). 'Its' without an apostrophe means '-nya', so 'Its new' is wrong.

steps.title: Never drop be
steps.text: This is the most important rule of the lesson.
steps.body: Indonesian often puts nothing in the middle: *Dia guru. Saya dari Surabaya. Ini tas saya.* English always needs **be** (the family **am / is**) after the **subject** (who or what the sentence is about). **I** takes **am**; **he, she, it, this** and names take **is**. So: *She teacher* ✗ → **She's a teacher** ✓. *I from Surabaya* ✗ → **I'm from Surabaya** ✓. *This my bag* ✗ → **This is my bag** ✓. **Budi is a student.**

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Find the sentence that keeps be.

question.prompt: Pak Joko seorang sopir. Which is correct?
question.explanation: After the subject (Pak Joko) comes **is**, then the job: **Pak Joko is a driver.** Without **is** the sentence is incomplete, and **is** can't go at the end.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Subject first, then be, then the rest.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Dia (laki-laki) guru saya.
question.explanation: Subject (**He**: who we talk about) + be (**is**) + the rest (**my teacher**). 'Dia guru saya' needs nothing in the middle, but English needs **is**. And *guru saya* → **my teacher** (*my* first).

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards and say the English before you check.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is a cheat sheet you can keep and look back at.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · First sentences with be
artifact.intro: English needs be (am / is) where Indonesian puts nothing in the middle. I → am; he, she, it, this, names → is. Use the short forms when you speak.
tips: Subject + **be** + the rest: *I'm* a student, *Rina is* my friend.
Show a thing with **This is …**, then describe it with **It's …**.

examples.en: This is my phone. It's black.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? This short video and reference page help.

id.greeting: Hai, selamat datang kembali! Hari ini kamu membuat kalimat bahasa Inggris pertamamu: siapa kamu, dari mana asalmu, dan benda apa itu. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: I'm = I am
steps.text: Kita mulai dari dirimu: nama dan kotamu.
steps.body: Bahasa Indonesia bilang *Saya Budi*, tanpa kata di tengahnya. Bahasa Inggris butuh **am** di situ (≈ *adalah*): **I am Budi**. Saat berbicara, biasanya digabung: **I'm** (tanda **'** menggantikan huruf *a*). Untuk kota atau negaramu, tambahkan **from**: **I'm from Bandung**. Sebelum pekerjaan, tambahkan **a** (≈ *seorang*): **I'm a student**. Bahasa Indonesia boleh tanpa *seorang*; bahasa Inggris tidak boleh tanpa **a**.

steps.title: Memperkenalkan diri
steps.text: Begini cara orang menyebut nama, pekerjaan dan kotanya.
steps.body: Setiap kalimat dimulai dengan **I'm**. Jangan cuma *I*.

examples.en: Hi, I'm Sari. I'm a teacher.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Susun kata-katanya dalam urutan bahasa Inggris. Siapa dulu, lalu dari mana.

question.explanation: Mulai dengan **I'm** (= I am), lalu **from** + nama kota. 'Saya dari Makassar' tidak butuh kata di antara *Saya* dan *dari*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **'m** (am).

steps.title: This is … dan It's …
steps.text: Sekarang kita bicara tentang benda di sekitarmu.
steps.body: *Ini kunci saya* tidak punya kata di antara *Ini* dan *kunci saya*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **is**: **This is my key.** Perhatikan urutannya: *kunci saya* → **my key** (*my* di depan). Pakai **This is** untuk menunjukkan sesuatu di dekatmu. Lalu jelaskan benda yang sama dengan **It's** (= it is): **It's small.** Hati-hati: **its** tanpa apostrof artinya '-nya' (milik sebuah benda), bukan 'it is'.

steps.title: Tunjukkan dan jelaskan
steps.text: Tunjukkan bendanya dulu dengan This is, lalu jelaskan dengan It's.
steps.body: **This is** menyebut bendanya. **It's** menjelaskan lebih lanjut.

examples.en: This is my phone. It's black.
This is my office. It's small.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Perhatikan setiap kalimat. Ada kata kecil **is**-nya? Apostrofnya benar?

question.prompt: Budi menunjukkan motor barunya. Mana yang benar?
options: This is my motorbike. It's new.
This is my motorbike. Its new.
question.explanation: Kedua kalimat butuh **is**: **This is** dan **It's** (= it is). 'Its' tanpa apostrof artinya '-nya', jadi 'Its new' salah.

steps.title: Jangan hilangkan be
steps.text: Ini aturan paling penting di pelajaran ini.
steps.body: Bahasa Indonesia sering tanpa kata di tengah: *Dia guru. Saya dari Surabaya. Ini tas saya.* Bahasa Inggris selalu butuh **be** (keluarga kata **am / is**) setelah **subjek** (siapa atau apa yang dibicarakan). **I** memakai **am**; **he, she, it, this** dan nama memakai **is**. Jadi: *She teacher* ✗ → **She's a teacher** ✓. *I from Surabaya* ✗ → **I'm from Surabaya** ✓. *This my bag* ✗ → **This is my bag** ✓. **Budi is a student.**

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Cari kalimat yang tetap memakai be.

question.prompt: Pak Joko seorang sopir. Mana yang benar?
question.explanation: Setelah subjek (Pak Joko) datang **is**, lalu pekerjaannya: **Pak Joko is a driver.** Tanpa **is** kalimatnya tidak lengkap, dan **is** tidak boleh di akhir.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Subjek dulu, lalu be, lalu sisanya.

question.explanation: Subjek (**He**: orang yang dibicarakan) + be (**is**) + sisanya (**my teacher**). 'Dia guru saya' tidak butuh kata di tengah, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **is**. Dan *guru saya* → **my teacher** (*my* di depan).

steps.title: Ulang cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya dan ucapkan bahasa Inggrisnya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini ringkasan yang bisa kamu simpan dan buka lagi kapan saja.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Kalimat pertama dengan be
artifact.intro: Bahasa Inggris butuh be (am / is) di tempat bahasa Indonesia tidak memakai kata apa pun di tengah kalimat. I → am; he, she, it, this, nama → is. Pakai bentuk pendek saat berbicara.
tips: Subjek + **be** + sisanya: *I'm* a student, *Rina is* my friend.
Tunjukkan benda dengan **This is …**, lalu jelaskan dengan **It's …**.

examples.en: This is my phone. It's black.

steps.title: Belajar lebih lanjut
steps.text: Mau latihan lagi? Video pendek dan halaman referensi ini bisa membantu.
